> One thing I don't think works currently is in the following scenario: During the global index 'cleanup', what will happen to the sessions reading it? I would assume that if the metadata has the old partition ids, then the index will be inconsistent with existing rows/partitions (since they are being deleted during the partitions are readable) I would also assume that if the metadata has the new partition ids, then the index will still have records not yet deleted to partitions that no-longer exists.
> 
> Note that we allow currentSchemaVersion and currentSchemaVersion-1 as valid schema versions!

@mjonss Please review this PR again.
I solved the problem by saving the original Definitions in a new data memeber `OriginalDeifnitions`.
- Read: `Definitions` in the metadata doesn't contain truncating definitions, so read is OK.
- Write: We can add check to ensure no record can be inserted into truncating definitions. How should we do it? We can locate partition in both `Defintions` and `OriginalDefinitions` in the metadata. If the result pids are different, we can ensure the write should be forbided.
e.g., 
`create table test_global (a int) partition by range( a ) ( partition p1 values less than (10), partition p2 values less than (20) );`
When execute `alter table test_global truncate partition p1;`, we should forbid `insert into test_global values (1);` stmt be executed. 
For `Definitions` in the metadata, (1) would be located in p2, while for `OriginalDefinitions` in the metadata, (1) would be located in p1. So this check enables no record can be inserted into truncating partitions.

>   For `Definitions` in the metadata, (1) would be located in p2, while for `OriginalDefinitions` in the metadata, (1) would be located in p1. So this check enables no record can be inserted into truncating partitions.

Will reading still work with named partitions, like `SELECT * FROM t PARTITION (pTruncated)`?
I don't think it is acceptable to start getting errors, or blocking writes, in an application that are reading and writing to a table, due to a concurrent `truncate partition`.

I would expect that either a session/transaction sees the partitions as before (if the Schema version is before the effective `truncate partition`) or sees the partitions as after (if the Schema version is after the effective `truncate partition`).

The trick would be to do the reorganization / update / cleaning of the global index transparent to both the before and the after Schema versions. I.e. that the sessions sees the before version, would have full access to the older partitions but not see any of the new partition ids, and the sessions that sees the after version does not see any of the old truncated ids, only the new ones. So during the in-place reorganization of the global index, there would need to be some kind of filter in place.

issue_context.title: ddl: truncate partition not handled correctly for global index
issue_context.body: ## Bug Report Please answer these questions before submitting your issue. Thanks! ### 1. Minimal reproduce step (Required) A unit test: ```golang func TestTruncatePartitionWithGlobalIndex(t *testing.T) { defer config.RestoreFunc()() config.UpdateGlobal(func(conf *config.Config) { conf.EnableGlobalIndex = true }) store := testkit.CreateMockStore(t) tk := testkit.NewTestKit(t, store) tk.MustExec("use test") tk.MustExec("drop table if exists test_global") tk.MustExec(`create table test_global ( a int, b int, c int) partition by range( a ) ( partition p1 values less than (10), partition p2 values less than (20) );`) tt := external.GetTableByName(t, tk, "test", "test_global") pid := tt.Meta().Partition.Definitions[1].ID tk.MustExec("Alter Table test_global Add Unique Index idx_b (b);") tk.MustExec("Alter Table test_global Add Unique Index idx_c (c);") tk.MustExec(`INSERT INTO test_global VALUES (1, 1, 1), (2, 2, 2), (11, 3, 3), (12, 4, 4)`) tk.MustExec("alter table test_global truncate partition p2;") result := tk.MustQuery("select * from test_global;") result.Sort().Check(testkit.Rows(`1 1 1`, `2 2 2`)) tt = external.GetTableByName(t, tk, "test", "test_global") idxInfo := tt.Meta().FindIndexByName("idx_b") require.NotNil(t, idxInfo) cnt := checkGlobalIndexCleanUpDone(t, tk.Session(), tt.Meta(), idxInfo, pid) require.Equal(t, 2, cnt) idxInfo = tt.Meta().FindIndexByName("idx_c") require.NotNil(t, idxInfo) cnt = checkGlobalIndexCleanUpDone(t, tk.Session(), tt.Meta(), idxInfo, pid) require.Equal(t, 2, cnt) } ``` ### 2. What did you expect to see? (Required) pass ### 3. What did you see instead (Required) failed, because global index rows was not cleaned. ### 4. What is your TiDB version? (Required)

review_comments: Should we simplify this if there are no global index and only have a single state change where the partitions will have the new ids? Or do we still need to go through the different stages?
`onDropTablePartition` also use Public->DeleteOnly->DeleteReorg 3 stages. Here I just stay the same. If you think it is necessary, I will improve the design.

Please add a check if there are any global indexes in the table, and if not, do a single state change, like `onTruncateTable()` (or like it was before this PR), then it will only affect global index usage, and the rest will behave just like before.

I think the `onDropTablePartition()` function could be optimized the same way, but let that be a separate optimization.

The goal should be user experience/behaviour of truncate partition with global index, be the same as truncate table or truncate partition without global index. What I would expect is that it would take some more time for index deletion, but not affect usage/transactions in any other way.
Same here, why expecting an error, I would expect it to succeed, from a users point of view.
Same here, I don't think it is expected by the users to get an error here.
If we canceled `ActionTruncateTablePartition` job, we should consider how to rollback it.

It will see `(2, 2, 2)` when truncate finished. This is not only inconsistent with the semantics of `delete only` state, and also inconsistent with comments `NewPartitionIDs is used to ensure no records can be inserted into new partitions when reorg.`

Why do we want an error here? (also it will fail even if there are no global index!)
I don't think this is expected by users.
Could add a comment here to indicates that the state of `DeleteOnly` is 'fake', and the insert into new partition can still be successful in this state.
